newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares ended higher on Friday lifted by bargain-hunting by a few investors, analysts said.
Most investors are stocking to the sidelines on uncertainty with most companies yet to release 1996 results, they said.
The B index gained 2.11 points or 1.30 percent to close at 164.25 points on thin turnover of HK$81.5 million, compared with Thursday's HK$104.2 million.
"The general mood is not great after the plunge on Thursday, but a few speculators have jumped in to pick up bargains," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
On Thursday, the B share index lost 3.29 percent to 162.14 points.
"Concerns over widespread talk of a looming securities clampdown and company annual results remain," a J&A Securities trader said.
Analysts said the movement of the index next week depended heavily on whether there was any announcement by Beijing on securities regulation.
Barring major news, the index is expected to edge higher on investor confidence over China's economic outlook, traders said.
But concern over 1996 results will cap gains, they said.
"Investors want to see what the annual results are before making decisions," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Only two out of 43 B share firms have published their annual reports so far, with the official April 30 deadline approaching.
Tsann Kuen Enterprise Co Ltd was the best performer, closing HK$0.15 or 3.66 percent at HK$4.25 on volume of 300,020 shares.
The A share index gained 10.84 points or 2.59 percent to 429.65 points on turnover of 8.73 billion yuan, compared with 9.6 billion yuan on Thursday.
